_meta.source: SEAB SEC 2027 syllabus listings (G1/G2/G3 school candidates), MOE course and applied subject pages, school Sec 3 option booklets. K codes verified by syllabus PDF title where marked confirmed.; MOE Full SBB pages and school FSBB briefings for the lower secondary model
_meta.notes: The national picture, not a promise about any one school. Schools run subsets, and the subjects marked selected are offered only at schools approved to run them. Teachers can trim the list to their school in the teacher layer. No syllabus codes are shown to students: the Combined Science pair to code mapping is unverified and the app never needs it. Items marked provisional could not be verified against a primary SEAB PDF title. Third languages (MOELC, PSLE gated) and MTL B (performance triggered) are deliberately not planner rows; see the availability sheet.

G1.label: G1
G1.name: General 1
G1.plain: The foundation, with a lot of practical work.

G2.label: G2
G2.name: General 2
G2.plain: Real depth, at a steadier pace.

availabilityNote.line: Schools offer different subsets of these. Refer to the combinations my school offers.
availabilityNote.sheet: Not every school runs every subject, and that is normal. Subjects tagged selected schools are approved at some schools only. A school's own subject list can also change between cohorts. Check mine on MOE SchoolFinder, at open house, or with my form teacher. Third languages run separately at the MOE Language Centre for eligible students, and MTL B exists for students who find Mother Tongue very heavy going; both are conversations with my school. At G3 the elective half of the Humanities pair can also be Literature in a Mother Tongue Language, at schools that run it.

groups.label: Science
groups.note: At G2, science comes as a pair. Single sciences are G3.

groups.label: Humanities
groups.note: At G2 and G3, one Humanities pair is part of the package. Single subjects can come on top.

groups.label: Everyone takes these too
groups.note: Common curriculum. Not levelled, and about a third of my week.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.doing: Work out what a writer is doing, then say it clearly.
subjects.likeIf: I like being the one who can explain it

subjects.name: Mother Tongue Language
subjects.doing: Read, write and hold a real conversation in my language.
subjects.likeIf: I already move between two worlds

subjects.name: Higher Mother Tongue
subjects.doing: The same language, taken further, with harder writing.
subjects.likeIf: the language is already a strength
subjects.note: Offered on strength in the language, usually beside a mostly G3 load. Ask my school.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.doing: Handle number, shape, chance and change, and spot a wrong answer.
subjects.likeIf: I like a problem I can check

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.doing: A second, harder Mathematics. Calculus and trigonometry taken further.
subjects.likeIf: Maths is what I would do anyway
subjects.caution: Worth taking because I like it, not to look strong.
subjects.keepsOpen: Poly counts Maths either way, Elementary or Additional.

subjects.name: Science
subjects.doing: Build it, test it, measure it, find out why it broke.
subjects.likeIf: I would rather find out by doing it

subjects.name: Science (Physics, Chemistry)
subjects.doing: Two sciences in one subject: forces and circuits beside reactions.
subjects.likeIf: I want science broad, with a technical lean
subjects.keepsOpen: Named in poly engineering, nursing and biomedical entry requirements.

subjects.name: Science (Physics, Biology)
subjects.doing: Two sciences in one subject: machines beside living things.
subjects.likeIf: I like both the lab and the field
subjects.keepsOpen: Named in poly engineering, nursing and biomedical entry requirements.

subjects.name: Science (Chemistry, Biology)
subjects.doing: Two sciences in one: what things are made of, alive and not.
subjects.likeIf: bodies, food and medicine pull at me
subjects.keepsOpen: Named in poly engineering, nursing and biomedical entry requirements.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.doing: Work out why things move, heat up and fall over.
subjects.likeIf: I take things apart to see inside
subjects.keepsOpen: Engineering never asks for Physics alone. Other sciences count too.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.doing: Find out what things are made of, and what reacts with what.
subjects.likeIf: I like a practical with a visible result

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.doing: Study living things, from one cell up to a whole forest.
subjects.likeIf: I am curious about bodies and disease

subjects.name: Humanities (Social Studies, Geography)
subjects.doing: How Singapore is governed, beside where people and water go.
subjects.likeIf: I want the map and the argument

subjects.name: Humanities (Social Studies, History)
subjects.doing: How Singapore is governed, beside sources that disagree about the past.
subjects.likeIf: I want to know who benefits from the story

subjects.name: Humanities (Social Studies, Literature in English)
subjects.doing: How Singapore is governed, beside reading closely enough to say something new.
subjects.likeIf: I have argued about what a film meant

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.doing: The full subject: people, water, weather and money, with fieldwork.
subjects.likeIf: I like maps, patterns and being outside

subjects.name: History
subjects.doing: The full subject: work from sources that disagree, build the argument.
subjects.likeIf: I argue back at documentaries

subjects.name: Literature in English
subjects.doing: The full subject: novels, plays and poems, read properly.
subjects.likeIf: books do things to me

subjects.name: Art
subjects.doing: Make work, defend it, and learn to look at other work properly.
subjects.likeIf: I already make things nobody asked for

subjects.name: Higher Art
subjects.doing: Art taken further, in the Art Elective Programme schools.
subjects.likeIf: art is the centre, not the side

subjects.name: Design and Technology
subjects.doing: Given a real problem, design and build the thing that solves it.
subjects.likeIf: I would rather hold a tool than a highlighter

subjects.name: Nutrition and Food Science
subjects.doing: Study what food is made of, and what it does in me.
subjects.likeIf: I cook, or want to know what I eat

subjects.name: Music
subjects.doing: Perform, compose, and hear what is going on inside a piece.
subjects.likeIf: I already play, write or produce

subjects.name: Higher Music
subjects.doing: Music taken further, in the Music Elective Programme schools.
subjects.likeIf: music is the centre, not the side

subjects.name: Principles of Accounts
subjects.doing: Learn how money moving through a business is recorded and read.
subjects.likeIf: I like things to balance

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.doing: Why prices, wages and shortages happen, argued with evidence.
subjects.likeIf: I ask why things cost what they cost
subjects.note: New at SEC, code K343, first exam 2027. Few schools run it yet. Ask mine.

subjects.name: Computing
subjects.doing: Write programs, work with data, and find out why software breaks.
subjects.likeIf: I like building what does not exist yet
subjects.note: Part of the G1 package from 2026. At G2 and G3, selected schools.

subjects.name: Elements of Business Skills
subjects.doing: Learn how a small business actually runs, day to day.
subjects.likeIf: I like people and being useful straight away

subjects.name: Exercise and Sports Science
subjects.doing: Study how the body performs, trains and recovers, and test it.
subjects.likeIf: sport is a serious part of my life

subjects.name: Drama
subjects.doing: Devise, rehearse and perform work, and analyse why it lands.
subjects.likeIf: I will be watched while getting it wrong

subjects.name: Electronics
subjects.doing: Build real circuits and find the fault when they stop.
subjects.likeIf: I like a soldering iron and a puzzle

subjects.name: Science
subjects.doing: One subject covering physics, chemistry and biology together.
subjects.likeIf: I want to know why things behave that way
subjects.note: At Sec 3 this becomes a pair, or a single science at G3.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.doing: How places work, and why people live where they do.
subjects.likeIf: maps and the shape of cities pull at me

subjects.name: History
subjects.doing: What happened, and how anyone knows that it did.
subjects.likeIf: I argue with the version I was handed

subjects.name: Literature in English
subjects.doing: Read closely, then say what the writer is actually doing.
subjects.likeIf: I notice how it is written, not just what
subjects.note: Some schools run this at lower secondary and some do not.

subjects.name: Art
subjects.doing: Make things, and look hard at things other people made.
subjects.likeIf: everyone takes it, so treat it as a look

subjects.name: Music
subjects.doing: Play, listen and work out how a piece holds together.
subjects.likeIf: everyone takes it, so treat it as a look

subjects.name: Design and Technology
subjects.doing: Design something, then actually build it.
subjects.likeIf: everyone takes it, so treat it as a look

subjects.name: Food and Consumer Education
subjects.doing: Cook, and understand what food is doing to me.
subjects.likeIf: everyone takes it, so treat it as a look

junctures.schoolNote: Schools set their own criteria and their own review points. My school's are the real ones.

sec1.up: English, Mother Tongue, Maths and Science can move up at the end of Sec 1.
sec1.note: Humanities levels start moving from Sec 2, not yet.

sec2.up: Everything on this list can move now, Humanities included.
sec2.note: End of Sec 2 sets the combination I carry into Sec 3.

sec3.note: Levels are largely settled now. What I do with them is not.

sec4.note: This year is about how I finish, not what level I finish at.

sec5.note: A fifth year widens what comes next. Aim it at something.

down.line: Levels can also be eased down.
down.body: Schools look at this when a subject is genuinely not sustainable, at the end of Sec 2 or Sec 3. It is done to protect the rest of my learning, never as a punishment for one hard year.
